source.text: כִּֽי־יִהְיֶ֥ה רִיב֙ בֵּ֣ין אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְנִגְּשׁ֥וּ אֶל־הַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט וּשְׁפָט֑וּם וְהִצְדִּ֨יקוּ֙ אֶת־הַצַּדִּ֔יק וְהִרְשִׁ֖יעוּ אֶת־הָרָשָֽׁע׃

records.literal_gloss: When there is [a] dispute between men, and they draw near to the judgment, and they judge them, and they declare righteous the righteous [one] and they declare guilty the guilty [one],

en.L: When there is a dispute between {{gender:people|men}}, and they come near to the judgment, and [the judges] judge them, and they declare the righteous [one] in the right and declare the guilty [one] guilty,
en.B: Suppose two people have a dispute and go to court, and the judges decide the case, declaring the one who is in the right innocent and the one who is in the wrong guilty.
en.R: Suppose two people have a quarrel and take it to court. The judges hear the case. They say that one person is innocent and the other is guilty.

es.L: Cuando haya un pleito entre {{gender:personas|hombres}}, y se acerquen al juicio, y [los jueces] los juzguen, y declaren justo al justo y declaren culpable al culpable,
es.B: Supongamos que dos personas tengan un pleito y acudan al tribunal, y que los jueces decidan el caso, declarando inocente al que tiene razón y culpable al que está en falta.
es.R: Supongamos que dos personas tienen una pelea y la llevan ante el tribunal. Los jueces escuchan el caso. Dicen que una persona es inocente y que la otra es culpable.

fr.L: Quand il y aura une contestation entre des {{gender:personnes|hommes}}, qu’ils s’approcheront du jugement et que [les juges] les jugeront, déclarant juste le juste et coupable le coupable,
fr.B: Supposons que deux personnes soient en litige et aillent en justice, et que les juges tranchent l’affaire, déclarant innocent celui qui a raison et coupable celui qui a tort.
fr.R: Supposons que deux personnes se disputent et portent l’affaire devant le tribunal. Les juges examinent le cas. Ils déclarent que l’un est innocent et que l’autre est coupable.

sw.L: Kukiwa na ugomvi kati ya watu, nao wakakaribia hukumu, na [waamuzi] wakawahukumu, wakamtangaza mwenye haki kuwa hana hatia, na mwenye hatia kuwa ana hatia,
sw.B: Tuseme watu wawili wana ugomvi, wakaenda mahakamani, na waamuzi wakaamua shauri lao, wakimtangaza asiye na hatia yule aliye na haki, na kumtangaza mwenye hatia yule aliyekosa.
sw.R: Tuseme watu wawili wanagombana, wakapeleka shauri lao mahakamani. Waamuzi wanasikiliza shauri hilo. Wanasema kwamba mmoja hana hatia na mwingine ana hatia.

decisions.choice: come near to the judgment: bring the case to court
decisions.reason: "The judgment" here is the place and act of judging: the case is taken before the judges in the town (16:18; 17:8-9; 19:17). The law begins with a dispute settled in court; the punishment that follows is given only after a verdict.

decisions.choice: declare the righteous in the right and the guilty guilty: give the verdict
decisions.reason: The two verbs are court words. They do not make someone righteous or wicked; they declare who is in the right and who is in the wrong in the case. The same pair stands in 1 Kings 8:32, and Proverbs 17:15 condemns judges who reverse them.

decisions.choice: men: the parties to the dispute, whoever they are
decisions.reason: The word is the plural of "man", but the law covers any two parties who bring a case. The verse sets the scene; the instruction itself comes in verses 2-3.

decisions.choice: [the judges]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they judge them" without naming who judges. Literal supplies "[the judges]" so the sentence can be followed; Balanced and Readable say "the judges" plainly.

decisions.choice: Suppose ... / and go to court
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable set out the case as a supposition and turn "come near to the judgment" into "go to court" or "take it to court" (m1).

source.text: וְהָיָ֛ה אִם־בִּ֥ן הַכּ֖וֹת הָרָשָׁ֑ע וְהִפִּיל֤וֹ הַשֹּׁפֵט֙ וְהִכָּ֣הוּ לְפָנָ֔יו כְּדֵ֥י רִשְׁעָת֖וֹ בְּמִסְפָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: and it will be, if a son of striking [is] the guilty [one], and will make him lie down the judge and will strike him before his face according to [the] sufficiency of his guilt by number.

en.L: then it shall be, if the guilty [one] deserves to be beaten, that the judge shall make him lie down and have him beaten in his presence, by number, according to his guilt.
en.B: If the guilty person deserves to be beaten, the judge is to make him lie down and have him flogged in his presence with the number of strokes his offense deserves.
en.R: If the guilty person should be punished by beating, the judge must have him lie down. Then he must be beaten while the judge watches. The number of blows must match how bad the wrong was.

es.L: entonces será que, si el culpable merece ser golpeado, el juez lo hará tenderse y lo hará golpear en su presencia, por número, conforme a su culpa.
es.B: Si el culpable merece ser castigado con golpes, el juez lo hará tenderse en el suelo y lo hará azotar en su presencia con el número de golpes que merezca su delito.
es.R: Si el culpable debe ser castigado con golpes, el juez debe hacer que se acueste en el suelo. Luego deben golpearlo mientras el juez mira. El número de golpes debe corresponder a lo grave que fue la falta.

fr.L: alors il arrivera, si le coupable mérite d’être battu, que le juge le fera coucher à terre et le fera frapper en sa présence, selon sa faute, d’un nombre [de coups].
fr.B: Si le coupable mérite d’être battu, le juge le fera étendre à terre et lui fera donner en sa présence le nombre de coups que mérite sa faute.
fr.R: Si le coupable doit être puni de coups, le juge le fera allonger par terre. Puis on le frappera sous les yeux du juge. Le nombre de coups doit correspondre à la gravité de sa faute.

sw.L: basi itakuwa, kama mwenye hatia anastahili kupigwa, mwamuzi atamlaza chini na kumfanya apigwe mbele yake, kwa hesabu, kulingana na hatia yake.
sw.B: Ikiwa mwenye hatia anastahili kupigwa, mwamuzi atamlaza chini na kuagiza apigwe mbele yake mapigo kwa idadi inayolingana na kosa lake.
sw.R: Ikiwa mwenye hatia anapaswa kuadhibiwa kwa kupigwa, mwamuzi lazima amlaze chini. Kisha lazima apigwe mwamuzi akiwa anaangalia. Idadi ya mapigo lazima ilingane na ubaya wa kosa lake.

decisions.choice: a son of striking: one who deserves a beating
decisions.reason: "Son of" with a noun describes a person by what belongs to him or what he has earned. "A son of death" is someone who deserves to die (1 Samuel 20:31; 26:16); "a son of striking" is someone whose offense calls for a beating.

decisions.choice: the judge makes him lie down and has him beaten in his presence
decisions.reason: The beating is a court punishment, carried out under the judge's eye, not a private act of revenge. The judge's presence keeps it within limits. The verb "strike" here, in the form used, means to have him struck; who did the striking is not said.

decisions.choice: according to his guilt, by number: a counted number of blows fitting the offense
decisions.reason: The blows are counted, and their number matches the wrong done. The punishment is measured, not left to the anger of the one who strikes. Verse 3 sets the limit.

decisions.choice: flogged / beaten
decisions.reason: Balanced says "flogged" for the beating ordered by the court; Readable keeps the plain "beaten". Neither names the tool, which the Hebrew does not.

source.text: אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יַכֶּ֖נּוּ לֹ֣א יֹסִ֑יף פֶּן־יֹסִ֨יף לְהַכֹּת֤וֹ עַל־אֵ֨לֶּה֙ מַכָּ֣ה רַבָּ֔ה וְנִקְלָ֥ה אָחִ֖יךָ לְעֵינֶֽיךָ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Forty he may strike him; not he will add, lest he add to strike him beyond these [a] blow much, and is dishonored your brother in your eyes.

en.L: Forty [blows] he may strike him; he shall not add [more], lest, if he should add to strike him beyond these with many blows, your brother be dishonored in your eyes.
en.B: He may be given up to forty strokes, but no more. If he were beaten with many more strokes than that, your fellow Israelite would be degraded in your sight.
en.R: He must not be given more than forty blows. If he got more than that, it would shame him, and you would no longer see your fellow Israelite with respect.

es.L: Cuarenta [golpes] podrá darle; no añadirá [más], no sea que, si añade a golpearlo más allá de estos con muchos golpes, tu hermano quede envilecido a tus ojos.
es.B: Podrán darle hasta cuarenta golpes, pero no más. Si lo golpearan con muchos más golpes, tu compatriota quedaría degradado ante tus ojos.
es.R: No se le deben dar más de cuarenta golpes. Si recibiera más, eso lo humillaría, y ya no verías con respeto a tu compatriota.

fr.L: Quarante [coups] il pourra le frapper ; il n’en ajoutera pas [plus], de peur que, s’il continuait à le frapper bien au-delà, de nombreux coups, ton frère ne soit avili à tes yeux.
fr.B: On pourra lui donner jusqu’à quarante coups, mais pas davantage. Si on le frappait de beaucoup plus de coups, cet Israélite, ton frère, serait avili à tes yeux.
fr.R: On ne doit pas lui donner plus de quarante coups. S’il en recevait davantage, ce serait l’humilier, et tu ne pourrais plus regarder avec respect cet autre Israélite.

sw.L: Mapigo arobaini anaweza kumpiga; asiongeze, asije akiongeza kumpiga mapigo mengi zaidi ya hayo, ndugu yako akadharauliwa machoni pako.
sw.B: Anaweza kupewa mapigo hadi arobaini, lakini si zaidi. Kama angepigwa mapigo mengi zaidi ya hayo, ndugu yako Mwisraeli angedhalilishwa machoni pako.
sw.R: Asipewe mapigo zaidi ya arobaini. Akipewa zaidi ya hayo, itamwaibisha, nawe hutamwona tena ndugu yako Mwisraeli kwa heshima.

decisions.choice: forty: the most that may be given, not a fixed number
decisions.reason: Forty is the upper limit; the judge sets the number by the offense (verse 2). In later times the count was stopped at thirty-nine, so as never to pass forty by a miscount; Paul says he received "forty less one" five times (2 Corinthians 11:24).

decisions.choice: be dishonored: be made worthless and contemptible
decisions.reason: The verb means to become light, of little weight, and so of no account. Even a guilty man is still "your brother". Punishment may hurt him, but it must not destroy his standing as a member of the people.

decisions.choice: in your eyes: in the sight of the people addressed
decisions.reason: "Your" is the whole people, spoken to as one. The concern is how Israel will see the punished man afterward.

decisions.choice: your fellow Israelite
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "fellow Israelite" for "your brother", which here means a member of the same people, as in 15:2. Literal keeps "your brother".

records.literal_gloss: Not you will muzzle [an] ox in its threshing.

en.L: You shall not muzzle an ox when it is threshing.
en.B: You must not muzzle an ox when it is treading out grain.
en.R: When an ox is walking on grain to separate it from the stalks, do not tie its mouth shut. Let it eat.

es.L: No pondrás bozal al buey cuando trille.
es.B: No debes ponerle bozal al buey mientras pisa el grano.
es.R: Cuando un buey camine sobre el grano para separarlo de la paja, no le amarres la boca. Déjalo comer.

fr.L: Tu ne muselleras pas le bœuf quand il dépique.
fr.B: Tu ne mettras pas de muselière au bœuf quand il foule le grain.
fr.R: Quand un bœuf marche sur les épis pour en séparer le grain, ne lui attache pas la bouche. Laisse-le manger.

sw.B: Usimfunge ng'ombe kinywa wakati anapokanyaga nafaka ili kuipura.
sw.R: Ng'ombe anapotembea juu ya nafaka ili kuitenganisha na mabua, usimfunge kinywa. Mwache ale.

decisions.choice: threshing: an ox walking over cut grain to loosen the kernels
decisions.reason: Cut grain was spread on a hard threshing floor, and oxen walked over it, or pulled a heavy board over it, to break the kernels loose from the stalks (Hosea 10:11; Isaiah 28:27-28). A muzzle would keep the working animal from eating any of the grain under its feet.

decisions.choice: cited in the New Testament for those who work for the gospel
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this verse twice. In 1 Corinthians 9:9-10 he argues from it that those who preach the gospel may rightly be supported by those they serve, and in 1 Timothy 5:18 he sets it beside the saying "the worker deserves his wages" to support elders who lead and teach.

decisions.choice: a law about animals among laws about people
decisions.reason: The verse stands alone, between laws on punishment (verses 1-3) and on a dead man's widow (verses 5-10). It is a short, general command, of the kind that may already have been a common saying: the one who labors should share in the harvest.

decisions.choice: walking on grain to separate it from the stalks / Let it eat.
decisions.reason: Readable explains what threshing is (m1) and states the point of the command, which is that the ox may eat while it works.

source.text: כִּֽי־יֵשְׁב֨וּ אַחִ֜ים יַחְדָּ֗ו וּמֵ֨ת אַחַ֤ד מֵהֶם֙ וּבֵ֣ן אֵֽין־ל֔וֹ לֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֧ה אֵֽשֶׁת־הַמֵּ֛ת הַח֖וּצָה לְאִ֣ישׁ זָ֑ר יְבָמָהּ֙ יָבֹ֣א עָלֶ֔יהָ וּלְקָחָ֥הּ ל֛וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֖ה וְיִבְּמָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: When dwell brothers together and dies one of them and [a] son there is not to him, not will be [the] wife of the dead [man] outside to a man strange; her husband's brother will go in to her and take her for himself as wife and perform the duty of a husband's brother to her.

en.L: When brothers live together, and one of them dies and has no son, the wife of the dead [man] shall not [be married] outside [the family] to a stranger. Her husband's brother shall go in to her and take her to himself as a wife and perform the duty of a husband's brother to her.
en.B: When brothers live together on the family land and one of them dies without a son, his widow must not be married to someone outside the family. Instead, her husband's brother shall marry her and so do for her the duty of a husband's brother.
en.R: Brothers may live near each other on their family's land. If one of them dies and has no son, his widow must not marry a man from outside the family. Her dead husband's brother must marry her. This is the duty a brother-in-law owes to his dead brother.

es.L: Cuando habiten hermanos juntos y muera uno de ellos y no tenga hijo, la mujer del muerto no [se casará] fuera [de la familia] con un hombre extraño. El hermano de su marido entrará a ella y la tomará para sí por mujer y cumplirá con ella el deber de cuñado.
es.B: Cuando unos hermanos vivan juntos en la tierra de la familia y uno de ellos muera sin dejar hijo, su viuda no debe casarse con alguien de fuera de la familia. El hermano de su marido se casará con ella y así cumplirá con ella el deber de cuñado.
es.R: Puede que unos hermanos vivan cerca unos de otros en la tierra de su familia. Si uno de ellos muere sin tener un hijo, su viuda no debe casarse con un hombre de otra familia. El hermano de su difunto marido tiene que casarse con ella. Ese es el deber que un cuñado tiene con su hermano muerto.

fr.L: Quand des frères habitent ensemble et que l’un d’eux meurt sans avoir de fils, la femme du mort ne se mariera pas au-dehors [de la famille] avec un homme étranger ; le frère de son mari ira vers elle, la prendra pour femme et accomplira envers elle le devoir de beau-frère.
fr.B: Quand des frères vivent ensemble sur la terre familiale et que l’un d’eux meurt sans laisser de fils, sa veuve ne doit pas épouser quelqu’un d’extérieur à la famille. C’est le frère de son mari qui l’épousera, remplissant ainsi envers elle le devoir de beau-frère.
fr.R: Des frères peuvent vivre près les uns des autres sur la terre de leur famille. Si l’un d’eux meurt sans avoir de fils, sa veuve ne doit pas épouser un homme d’une autre famille. Le frère de son mari défunt doit l’épouser. C’est le devoir qu’un beau-frère a envers son frère mort.

sw.L: Ndugu wakikaa pamoja, na mmoja wao akafa bila kuwa na mwana, mke wa marehemu asiolewe nje [ya jamaa] na mwanamume mgeni; ndugu wa mumewe ataingia kwake na kumtwaa kuwa mke wake, na kumtimizia wajibu wa shemeji.
sw.B: Ndugu wakiishi pamoja katika ardhi ya jamaa yao, na mmoja wao akafa bila kuacha mwana, mjane wake asiolewe na mtu wa nje ya jamaa. Badala yake, ndugu wa mumewe atamwoa, na hivyo kumtimizia wajibu wa shemeji.
sw.R: Ndugu wanaweza kuishi karibu karibu katika ardhi ya jamaa yao. Mmoja wao akifa bila kuwa na mwana, mjane wake asiolewe na mwanamume wa jamaa nyingine. Ndugu wa marehemu mumewe lazima amwoe. Huo ndio wajibu ambao shemeji anao kwa ndugu yake aliyekufa.

decisions.choice: the duty of a husband's brother: the custom known as levirate marriage
decisions.reason: When a married man died without a son, his brother was to marry the widow, and the first son born to them counted as the dead man's son (verse 6). The custom is older than this law: Judah tells Onan to do this duty for Tamar (Genesis 38:8-10). Ruth 4 shows the same concern for a dead man's name and land, carried out by a more distant relative, Boaz, who marries Ruth "to raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance" (Ruth 4:5, 10). The name "levirate" comes from the Latin word for a husband's brother.

decisions.choice: live together: share the family's land, perhaps not yet divided
decisions.reason: The brothers live on the same family holding. The law has in view the land and name of one family; it does not bind a brother who lives far away. The widow stays with the family into which she married, and the dead man's share of the land stays in his line.

decisions.choice: a son: a male heir
decisions.reason: The word is "son". A man's land passed to his sons, and to his daughters if he had no son (Numbers 27:8). The ancient Greek translation reads "offspring" here, which would include a daughter; the Hebrew says "son".

decisions.choice: outside, to a strange man: to a man who is not of the family
decisions.reason: "Strange" here means an outsider to this family, not a foreigner or a wicked man. If she married outside, the dead man's land would go with her to another household.

decisions.choice: a brother-in-law
decisions.reason: Readable says "brother-in-law" for "husband's brother", as Genesis 38:8 does, and explains the duty as one owed to the dead brother (verse 6). Literal and Balanced keep "husband's brother".

decisions.choice: el hermano de su marido; el deber de cuñado
decisions.reason: Spanish names the duty with "cuñado", as Genesis 38:8 does; "el hermano de su marido" keeps the Hebrew "her husband's brother" for the man himself, and Readable calls him "un cuñado".

decisions.choice: le frère de son mari; le devoir de beau-frère
decisions.reason: French names the duty with "beau-frère", as Genesis 38:8 does; "le frère de son mari" keeps the Hebrew "her husband's brother" for the man himself, and Readable calls him "un beau-frère".

decisions.choice: ndugu wa mumewe; wajibu wa shemeji
decisions.reason: Swahili names the duty with "shemeji", as Genesis 38:8 does; "ndugu wa mumewe" keeps the Hebrew "her husband's brother" for the man himself.

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה הַבְּכוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֵּלֵ֔ד יָק֕וּם עַל־שֵׁ֥ם אָחִ֖יו הַמֵּ֑ת וְלֹֽא־יִמָּחֶ֥ה שְׁמ֖וֹ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, the firstborn whom she bears will stand on [the] name of his brother, the dead [one], and not will be wiped out his name from Israel.

en.L: And it shall be [that] the firstborn whom she bears shall stand on the name of his dead brother, so that his name shall not be wiped out from Israel.
en.B: The first son she bears shall bear the dead brother's name, so that the dead man's name is not wiped out from Israel.
en.R: Her first son will be counted as the dead man's son. That way the dead man's family name will not disappear from Israel.

es.L: Y será [que] el primogénito que ella dé a luz se levantará sobre el nombre de su hermano muerto, para que no sea borrado su nombre de Israel.
es.B: El primer hijo que ella dé a luz llevará el nombre del hermano muerto, para que el nombre del difunto no sea borrado de Israel.
es.R: Su primer hijo será contado como hijo del muerto. Así el nombre de la familia del muerto no desaparecerá de Israel.

fr.L: Et il arrivera que le premier-né qu’elle enfantera se lèvera sur le nom de son frère mort, pour que son nom ne soit pas effacé d’Israël.
fr.B: Le premier fils qu’elle mettra au monde portera le nom du frère défunt, afin que le nom du mort ne soit pas effacé d’Israël.
fr.R: Son premier fils sera compté comme le fils du mort. Ainsi le nom de famille du mort ne disparaîtra pas d’Israël.

sw.L: Na itakuwa kwamba mzaliwa wa kwanza atakayemzaa atasimama juu ya jina la ndugu yake aliyekufa, ili jina lake lisifutwe katika Israeli.
sw.B: Mwana wa kwanza atakayemzaa atalibeba jina la ndugu aliyekufa, ili jina la marehemu lisifutike katika Israeli.
sw.R: Mwana wake wa kwanza atahesabiwa kuwa mwana wa marehemu. Kwa njia hiyo jina la ukoo wa marehemu halitatoweka katika Israeli.

decisions.choice: stand on the name of his brother: succeed to the dead man's name and inheritance
decisions.reason: The child is reckoned as the dead man's son. He carries his name in the family line and receives his share of the land, which is what "name" means here (Ruth 4:5, 10; Numbers 27:4). "His brother" is the brother of the man who fathers the child.

decisions.choice: the firstborn: the first son she bears
decisions.reason: Only the first son is counted to the dead man; children born after him belong to their father.

decisions.choice: his name not wiped out from Israel: his line kept among God's people
decisions.reason: To have one's name blotted out was to vanish from the people as if one had never been (9:14; 29:19). The law keeps a place in Israel, and in the land given to Israel, for a man who died before he had a son.

decisions.choice: will be counted as the dead man's son
decisions.reason: Readable states what "stand on the name of his brother" means (m1).

source.text: וְאִם־לֹ֤א יַחְפֹּץ֙ הָאִ֔ישׁ לָקַ֖חַת אֶת־יְבִמְתּ֑וֹ וְעָלְתָה֩ יְבִמְתּ֨וֹ הַשַּׁ֜עְרָה אֶל־הַזְּקֵנִ֗ים וְאָֽמְרָה֙ מֵאֵ֨ין יְבָמִ֜י לְהָקִ֨ים לְאָחִ֥יו שֵׁם֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה יַבְּמִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And if not desires the man to take his brother's wife, then will go up his brother's wife to the gate, to the elders, and say, refuses my husband's brother to raise up for his brother [a] name in Israel; not he is willing to perform the duty of a husband's brother to me.

en.L: But if the man does not want to take his brother's wife, then his brother's wife shall go up to the gate, to the elders, and say, 'My husband's brother refuses to raise up a name for his brother in Israel; he is not willing to perform the duty of a husband's brother to me.'
en.B: But if the man is unwilling to marry his brother's widow, she shall go up to the elders at the town gate and say, 'My husband's brother refuses to keep his brother's name alive in Israel. He will not do the duty of a husband's brother for me.'
en.R: But the brother may not want to marry his brother's widow. Then she must go to the town leaders at the city gate. She must tell them, 'My brother-in-law will not keep my dead husband's family name alive in Israel. He refuses to do his duty and marry me.'

es.L: Pero si el hombre no quiere tomar a la mujer de su hermano, la mujer de su hermano subirá a la puerta, a los ancianos, y dirá: “El hermano de mi marido se niega a levantar un nombre para su hermano en Israel; no quiere cumplir conmigo el deber de cuñado”.
es.B: Pero si el hombre no quiere casarse con la viuda de su hermano, ella subirá a donde están los ancianos, a la puerta de la ciudad, y dirá: “El hermano de mi marido se niega a mantener vivo el nombre de su hermano en Israel. No quiere cumplir conmigo el deber de cuñado”.
es.R: Pero puede que el hermano no quiera casarse con la viuda de su hermano. Entonces ella debe ir a ver a los líderes de la ciudad, a la puerta de la ciudad. Debe decirles: “Mi cuñado no quiere mantener vivo en Israel el nombre de la familia de mi difunto marido. Se niega a cumplir su deber y casarse conmigo”.

fr.L: Mais si l’homme ne veut pas prendre la femme de son frère, la femme de son frère montera à la porte, vers les anciens, et dira : “Le frère de mon mari refuse de relever le nom de son frère en Israël ; il ne veut pas accomplir envers moi le devoir de beau-frère.”
fr.B: Mais si cet homme refuse d’épouser la veuve de son frère, elle montera trouver les anciens à la porte de la ville et dira : “Le frère de mon mari refuse de garder vivant le nom de son frère en Israël. Il ne veut pas remplir envers moi le devoir de beau-frère.”
fr.R: Mais il peut arriver que le frère ne veuille pas épouser la veuve de son frère. Elle doit alors aller trouver les responsables de la ville, à la porte de la ville. Elle leur dira : “Mon beau-frère ne veut pas garder vivant en Israël le nom de famille de mon mari mort. Il refuse de faire son devoir et de m’épouser.”

sw.L: Lakini kama mtu huyo hapendi kumtwaa mke wa ndugu yake, basi mke wa ndugu yake atakwea langoni kwa wazee, na kusema, 'Ndugu wa mume wangu anakataa kumwinulia ndugu yake jina katika Israeli; hataki kunitimizia wajibu wa shemeji.'
sw.B: Lakini kama mwanamume huyo hataki kumwoa mjane wa ndugu yake, mjane huyo atakwenda kwa wazee kwenye lango la mji na kusema, 'Ndugu wa mume wangu anakataa kulidumisha jina la ndugu yake katika Israeli. Hataki kunitimizia wajibu wa shemeji.'
sw.R: Lakini huenda ndugu huyo hataki kumwoa mjane wa ndugu yake. Basi mjane lazima aende kwa viongozi wa mji kwenye lango la mji. Lazima awaambie, 'Shemeji yangu hataki kulidumisha katika Israeli jina la ukoo wa marehemu mume wangu. Anakataa kutimiza wajibu wake na kunioa.'

decisions.choice: the gate, the elders: the town's court
decisions.reason: Cases were heard at the town gate, where people passed and met, before the older men who led the town (21:19; 22:15; Ruth 4:1-2). The widow brings her complaint there herself, in public.

decisions.choice: does not want: the brother may refuse
decisions.reason: The law does not force the brother to marry the widow. It lets him refuse, but only openly and at the cost of public shame (verses 8-10).

decisions.choice: raise up a name for his brother: provide his brother with an heir
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, the "name" is the dead man's place in the family line and his share of the land.

decisions.choice: town leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says "town leaders" for "the elders", who were the older men leading the town, and adds what the duty is ("marry me").

decisions.choice: his brother's widow
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "widow" for "his brother's wife", since her husband is dead. Literal keeps "wife".

source.text: וְקָֽרְאוּ־ל֥וֹ זִקְנֵי־עִיר֖וֹ וְדִבְּר֣וּ אֵלָ֑יו וְעָמַ֣ד וְאָמַ֔ר לֹ֥א חָפַ֖צְתִּי לְקַחְתָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will call him [the] elders of his city and speak to him, and he stands and says, not I desire to take her,

en.L: And the elders of his city shall call him and speak to him; and [if] he stands [firm] and says, 'I do not want to take her,'
en.B: Then the elders of his town are to summon him and speak with him. If he holds to his refusal and says, 'I do not want to marry her,'
en.R: Then the leaders of his town must call for him and talk with him. But he may still say, 'I do not want to marry her.'

es.L: Y los ancianos de su ciudad lo llamarán y le hablarán; y [si] él se mantiene [firme] y dice: “No quiero tomarla”,
es.B: Entonces los ancianos de su ciudad lo llamarán y hablarán con él. Si se mantiene en su negativa y dice: “No quiero casarme con ella”,
es.R: Entonces los líderes de su ciudad deben llamarlo y hablar con él. Pero puede que él siga diciendo: “No quiero casarme con ella”.

fr.L: Et les anciens de sa ville l’appelleront et lui parleront ; et [s’]il se tient [ferme] et dit : “Je ne veux pas la prendre”,
fr.B: Alors les anciens de sa ville le convoqueront et lui parleront. S’il maintient son refus et dit : “Je ne veux pas l’épouser”,
fr.R: Alors les responsables de sa ville doivent le faire venir et lui parler. Mais il peut dire encore : “Je ne veux pas l’épouser.”

sw.L: Ndipo wazee wa mji wake watamwita na kusema naye; na [kama] atasimama [imara] na kusema, 'Sipendi kumtwaa,'
sw.B: Kisha wazee wa mji wake watamwita na kuzungumza naye. Kama ataendelea kukataa na kusema, 'Sitaki kumwoa,'
sw.R: Kisha viongozi wa mji wake lazima wamwite na kuzungumza naye. Lakini huenda bado akasema, 'Sitaki kumwoa.'

decisions.choice: he stands: he holds to his position
decisions.reason: "Stand" here means to remain where he is, firm in his refusal after the elders have spoken. The sentence goes on into verse 9, which says what follows.

decisions.choice: the elders speak to him: they try to persuade him
decisions.reason: The elders hear him and urge him to do his duty. They do not compel him.

decisions.choice: [if] ... [firm]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words English needs to show that this is a condition and what "stands" means (m1).

source.text: וְנִגְּשָׁ֨ה יְבִמְתּ֣וֹ אֵלָיו֮ לְעֵינֵ֣י הַזְּקֵנִים֒ וְחָלְצָ֤ה נַעֲלוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל רַגְל֔וֹ וְיָרְקָ֖ה בְּפָנָ֑יו וְעָֽנְתָה֙ וְאָ֣מְרָ֔ה כָּ֚כָה יֵעָשֶׂ֣ה לָאִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יִבְנֶ֖ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית אָחִֽיו

records.literal_gloss: then will draw near his brother's wife to him before [the] eyes of the elders and draw off his sandal from on his foot and spit in his face and answer and say, thus will be done to the man who not builds [the] house of his brother.

en.L: then his brother's wife shall come near to him in the sight of the elders, and pull his sandal off his foot, and spit in his face; and she shall answer and say, 'So shall it be done to the man who does not build up his brother's house.'
en.B: then his brother's widow is to go up to him in front of the elders, pull his sandal off his foot and spit in his face. She shall then declare, 'So it shall be done to any man who refuses to build up his brother's family.'
en.R: Then, while the leaders watch, the widow must go up to him. She must pull one of his sandals off his foot and spit in his face. Then she must say, 'This is what happens to a man who will not give his brother a family.'

es.L: entonces la mujer de su hermano se acercará a él a los ojos de los ancianos, le quitará la sandalia del pie y le escupirá en la cara; y responderá y dirá: “Así se hará al hombre que no edifica la casa de su hermano”.
es.B: entonces la viuda de su hermano se acercará a él delante de los ancianos, le quitará la sandalia del pie y le escupirá en la cara. Luego declarará: “Así se hace con el hombre que se niega a levantar la familia de su hermano”.
es.R: Entonces, mientras los líderes miran, la viuda debe acercarse a él. Debe quitarle una de sus sandalias y escupirle en la cara. Luego debe decir: “Esto es lo que le pasa al hombre que no quiere darle una familia a su hermano”.

fr.L: alors la femme de son frère s’approchera de lui sous les yeux des anciens, lui retirera sa sandale du pied et lui crachera au visage ; et elle prendra la parole et dira : “Ainsi sera-t-il fait à l’homme qui ne bâtit pas la maison de son frère.”
fr.B: alors la veuve de son frère s’avancera vers lui en présence des anciens, lui ôtera sa sandale du pied et lui crachera au visage. Puis elle déclarera : “Voilà ce qu’on fait à l’homme qui refuse de bâtir la famille de son frère.”
fr.R: Alors, sous les yeux des responsables, la veuve doit s’approcher de lui. Elle doit lui retirer une de ses sandales et lui cracher au visage. Puis elle doit dire : “Voilà ce qui arrive à l’homme qui ne veut pas donner une famille à son frère.”

sw.L: ndipo mke wa ndugu yake atamkaribia mbele ya macho ya wazee, na kumvua kubazi lake mguuni mwake, na kumtemea mate usoni; naye atajibu na kusema, 'Ndivyo atakavyotendewa mtu asiyeijenga nyumba ya ndugu yake.'
sw.B: ndipo mjane wa ndugu yake atamwendea mbele ya wazee, amvue kubazi lake mguuni na kumtemea mate usoni. Kisha atatangaza, 'Ndivyo anavyotendewa mtu anayekataa kuijenga jamaa ya ndugu yake.'
sw.R: Kisha, viongozi wakiwa wanaangalia, mjane lazima amwendee. Lazima amvue kubazi lake moja mguuni na kumtemea mate usoni. Kisha lazima aseme, 'Hivi ndivyo inavyompata mwanamume asiyetaka kumpa ndugu yake jamaa.'

decisions.choice: pull his sandal off his foot: a sign that he gives up his right and duty
decisions.reason: A sandal was used in giving up or handing over a right. Ruth 4:7-8 explains that in Israel a man took off his sandal and gave it to another to confirm a transfer of rights. Here the widow takes it from him: he has refused his place in his brother's family, and she is free of any claim he had. Planting a sandal on land could also be a sign of taking possession (Psalm 60:10).

decisions.choice: spit in his face: a public mark of disgrace
decisions.reason: To spit in someone's face was to shame them openly (Numbers 12:14; Isaiah 50:6). Later Jewish practice had the widow spit on the ground in front of him, and the words can be read "before him", but the plain sense is "in his face".

decisions.choice: build up his brother's house: give his brother a family line
decisions.reason: "House" means a household and a line of descendants, as when the LORD promises to build David a house (2 Samuel 7:27). Ruth 4:11 uses the same picture of Rachel and Leah, who "built the house of Israel".

decisions.choice: one of his sandals
decisions.reason: Readable says "one of his sandals", since the Hebrew "his sandal" names a single sandal from one foot.

source.text: וְנִקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בֵּ֖ית חֲל֥וּץ הַנָּֽעַל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And will be called his name in Israel, [the] house of [the one] drawn off of the sandal.

en.L: And his name shall be called in Israel, 'The house of the one whose sandal was pulled off.'
en.B: And his family will be known in Israel as 'The family of the man whose sandal was pulled off.'
en.R: From then on, his family will be known in Israel as 'The family of the man who had his sandal pulled off.'

es.L: Y será llamado su nombre en Israel: “La casa de aquel a quien quitaron la sandalia”.
es.B: Y su familia será conocida en Israel como “la familia del hombre al que le quitaron la sandalia”.
es.R: Desde ese día, en Israel llamarán a su familia “la familia del hombre que se quedó sin sandalia”.

fr.L: Et son nom sera appelé en Israël : “La maison de celui à qui on a retiré la sandale.”
fr.B: Et sa famille sera connue en Israël sous le nom de “la famille de l’homme à qui on a retiré sa sandale”.
fr.R: Dès lors, en Israël, on appellera sa famille “la famille de l’homme qui s’est fait enlever sa sandale”.

sw.L: Na jina lake litaitwa katika Israeli, 'Nyumba ya yule aliyevuliwa kubazi.'
sw.B: Na jamaa yake itajulikana katika Israeli kama, 'Jamaa ya mtu aliyevuliwa kubazi.'
sw.R: Tangu hapo, jamaa yake itajulikana katika Israeli kama 'Jamaa ya mwanamume aliyevuliwa kubazi lake.'

decisions.choice: his name: the name of his house, his family
decisions.reason: "His name" can refer to the man or to his house; the name given is the name of his household. The family that would not build up a brother's house is itself named by its refusal.

decisions.choice: the house of the one drawn off of the sandal: a name of reproach
decisions.reason: The name keeps the shame of the scene in verse 9 attached to his family. The punishment is public dishonor, not a fine or a beating.

decisions.choice: his family will be known / The family of
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "family" for "house", as in verse 9, and "be known as" for "his name shall be called".

source.text: כִּֽי־יִנָּצ֨וּ אֲנָשִׁ֤ים יַחְדָּו֙ אִ֣ישׁ וְאָחִ֔יו וְקָֽרְבָה֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת הָֽאֶחָ֔ד לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶת־אִישָׁ֖הּ מִיַּ֣ד מַכֵּ֑הוּ וְשָׁלְחָ֣ה יָדָ֔הּ וְהֶחֱזִ֖יקָה בִּמְבֻשָֽׁיו׃

records.literal_gloss: When struggle men together, a man and his brother, and draws near [the] wife of the one to rescue her husband from [the] hand of [the one] striking him, and she stretches out her hand and seizes [him] by his private parts,

en.L: When men are fighting together, a man and his brother, and the wife of the one comes near to rescue her husband from the hand of the one striking him, and she puts out her hand and seizes [him] by his private parts,
en.B: If two men are fighting each other and the wife of one of them comes up to rescue her husband from the man who is hitting him, and she reaches out and grabs the other man by his private parts,
en.R: Suppose two men are fighting, and the wife of one of them comes to help her husband against the man who is hitting him. She reaches out and grabs that man by his private parts.

es.L: Cuando peleen hombres juntos, un hombre y su hermano, y se acerque la mujer del uno para librar a su marido de la mano del que lo golpea, y extienda su mano y [lo] agarre por sus partes vergonzosas,
es.B: Si dos hombres se están peleando y la mujer de uno de ellos se acerca para librar a su marido del que lo golpea, y extiende la mano y agarra al otro hombre por sus partes íntimas,
es.R: Supongamos que dos hombres se pelean, y la mujer de uno de ellos viene a ayudar a su marido contra el hombre que lo golpea. Ella extiende la mano y agarra a ese hombre por sus partes íntimas.

fr.L: Quand des hommes se battent ensemble, un homme et son frère, et que la femme de l’un s’approche pour délivrer son mari de la main de celui qui le frappe, et qu’elle avance la main et [le] saisit par ses parties honteuses,
fr.B: Si deux hommes se battent et que la femme de l’un d’eux s’approche pour délivrer son mari de celui qui le frappe, et qu’elle tend la main et saisit l’autre homme par ses parties intimes,
fr.R: Supposons que deux hommes se battent, et que la femme de l’un d’eux vienne aider son mari contre l’homme qui le frappe. Elle tend la main et saisit cet homme par ses parties intimes.

sw.L: Wanaume wakipigana pamoja, mtu na ndugu yake, na mke wa mmoja wao akakaribia ili kumwokoa mumewe mkononi mwa yule anayempiga, naye akanyosha mkono wake na kumkamata [yule] sehemu zake za siri,
sw.B: Wanaume wawili wakipigana, na mke wa mmoja wao akaja kumwokoa mumewe kutoka kwa yule anayempiga, naye akanyosha mkono na kumkamata yule mwanamume mwingine sehemu zake za siri,
sw.R: Tuseme wanaume wawili wanapigana, na mke wa mmoja wao anakuja kumsaidia mumewe dhidi ya mwanamume anayempiga. Ananyosha mkono wake na kumkamata mwanamume huyo sehemu zake za siri.

decisions.choice: private parts: the male genitals
decisions.reason: The word means "the shameful parts", from a verb meaning to be ashamed. It is a discreet way of naming the genitals. Her act is not only an assault but a shameful one, and could rob the man of his ability to father children.

decisions.choice: a man and his brother: one man and another
decisions.reason: "A man and his brother" is a common way of saying "one another" (Exodus 25:20); it does not mean the two are brothers by birth.

decisions.choice: she comes to rescue her husband: her aim is to help him
decisions.reason: The law grants that she means to save her husband from harm. Even so, verse 12 says that this way of doing it is not to be excused. The sentence runs on into verse 12.

decisions.choice: the other man / that man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name whose parts she seizes, which the Hebrew leaves to "his". Literal brackets "[him]".

records.literal_gloss: then you will cut off her palm; not will look with pity your eye.

en.L: then you shall cut off her hand; your eye shall not pity [her].
en.B: then you must cut off her hand. Show her no pity.
en.R: Then you must cut off her hand. Do not feel sorry for her.

es.L: le cortarás la mano; tu ojo no tendrá piedad [de ella].
es.B: deberás cortarle la mano. No le tengas compasión.
es.R: Entonces tienes que cortarle la mano. No sientas lástima por ella.

fr.L: tu lui couperas la main ; ton œil n’aura pas pitié [d’elle].
fr.B: tu devras lui couper la main. Ne lui montre aucune pitié.
fr.R: Alors tu dois lui couper la main. Ne t’apitoie pas sur elle.

sw.L: utaukata mkono wake; jicho lako lisimhurumie.
sw.B: utaukata mkono wake. Usimwonee huruma yoyote.
sw.R: Basi lazima ukate mkono wake. Usimhurumie.

decisions.choice: cut off her hand: a bodily punishment, set by the court
alternatives: pay a fine for the shame caused
decisions.reason: This is the only place in the law of Moses where a part of the body is cut off as a punishment for a person. The "you" is Israel acting through its judges, as in verses 1-3. The word is "palm", the open hand with which she seized him. Later Jewish interpretation took the punishment as a payment for the shame caused; the words themselves speak of cutting off the hand.

decisions.choice: your eye shall not pity: show no mercy that sets the sentence aside
decisions.reason: The same words are said of the false prophet and the murderer (13:9; 19:13, 21). The judges are not to let pity for her, or her good aim, cancel the penalty.

decisions.choice: Show her no pity / Do not feel sorry for her
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "your eye shall not pity" into a direct command and name her as the one not to be pitied.

source.text: לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ בְּכִֽיסְךָ֖ אֶ֣בֶן וָאָ֑בֶן גְּדוֹלָ֖ה וּקְטַנָּֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Not will be to you in your bag [a] stone and [a] stone, large and small.

en.L: You shall not have in your bag a stone and a stone, a large and a small.
en.B: You must not carry two different weights in your bag, one heavy and one light.
en.R: Do not keep two sets of weights in your bag, one heavy and one light.

es.L: No tendrás en tu bolsa piedra y piedra, una grande y una pequeña.
es.B: No debes llevar en tu bolsa dos pesas distintas, una pesada y otra ligera.
es.R: No guardes en tu bolsa dos juegos de pesas, uno pesado y otro liviano.

fr.L: Tu n’auras pas dans ton sac pierre et pierre, une grande et une petite.
fr.B: Tu ne dois pas avoir dans ton sac deux poids différents, un lourd et un léger.
fr.R: Ne garde pas dans ton sac deux sortes de poids, l’un lourd et l’autre léger.

sw.L: Usiwe na mfukoni mwako jiwe na jiwe, kubwa na dogo.
sw.B: Usibebe mfukoni mwako mawe mawili tofauti ya kupimia, moja zito na jingine jepesi.
sw.R: Usiweke mfukoni mwako aina mbili za mawe ya kupimia uzito, moja zito na jingine jepesi.

decisions.choice: a stone and a stone: two weights for the same unit
decisions.reason: Goods and silver were weighed on a balance against stones of a set weight, carried in a pouch (Proverbs 16:11; Micah 6:11). A dishonest trader kept two stones for the same weight: a heavy one for weighing what he bought and a light one for what he sold. Amos 8:5 condemns the same trick.

decisions.choice: a stone and a stone: the repetition means two kinds
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats a word to mean "two different" ones (Psalm 12:3 says "a heart and a heart" for a double heart). The point is not that a trader owns two sizes of weight, but that he has two different stones for what should be one weight.

decisions.choice: two different weights, one heavy and one light
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "weights" for "stones" and "heavy and light" for "large and small", which is what the difference meant on a balance. Literal keeps "stone".

source.text: לֹא־יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ בְּבֵיתְךָ֖ אֵיפָ֣ה וְאֵיפָ֑ה גְּדוֹלָ֖ה וּקְטַנָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Not will be to you in your house [an] ephah and [an] ephah, large and small.

en.L: You shall not have in your house an ephah and an ephah, a large and a small.
en.B: You must not keep two different grain measures in your house, one large and one small.
en.R: Do not keep two different baskets for measuring grain in your house, one large and one small.

es.L: No tendrás en tu casa efa y efa, uno grande y uno pequeño.
es.B: No debes tener en tu casa dos medidas de grano distintas, una grande y otra pequeña.
es.R: No guardes en tu casa dos canastas distintas para medir el grano, una grande y otra pequeña.

fr.L: Tu n’auras pas dans ta maison épha et épha, un grand et un petit.
fr.B: Tu ne dois pas garder chez toi deux mesures à grain différentes, une grande et une petite.
fr.R: Ne garde pas dans ta maison deux paniers différents pour mesurer le grain, un grand et un petit.

sw.L: Usiwe na nyumbani mwako efa na efa, kubwa na ndogo.
sw.B: Usiweke nyumbani mwako vipimo viwili tofauti vya nafaka, kimoja kikubwa na kingine kidogo.
sw.R: Usiweke nyumbani mwako vikapu viwili tofauti vya kupimia nafaka, kimoja kikubwa na kingine kidogo.

decisions.choice: an ephah: a container for measuring grain
decisions.reason: The ephah was a dry measure, about 20 quarts, and also the basket or vessel that held that amount. Here it is the measuring vessel itself. A trader with a large and a small ephah could take in more grain than he paid for and give out less than he was paid for (Amos 8:5; Micah 6:10).

decisions.choice: two different grain measures / baskets for measuring grain
decisions.reason: The point is the vessel, not its size, so Balanced and Readable name what it was used for and give no modern measure. Literal keeps "ephah".

source.text: אֶ֣בֶן שְׁלֵמָ֤ה וָצֶ֨דֶק֙ יִֽהְיֶה־לָּ֔ךְ אֵיפָ֧ה שְׁלֵמָ֛ה וָצֶ֖דֶק יִֽהְיֶה־לָּ֑ךְ לְמַ֨עַן֙ יַאֲרִ֣יכוּ יָמֶ֔יךָ עַ֚ל הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] stone full and righteous will be to you, [an] ephah full and righteous will be to you, so that may be long your days on the land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you.

en.L: A full and right stone you shall have; a full and right ephah you shall have, so that your days may be long on the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you.
en.B: You must have weights that are complete and honest, and measures that are complete and honest, so that you may live long in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you.
en.R: Your weights and your measures must be honest and the right size. Then you will live a long time in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you.

es.L: Piedra entera y justa tendrás; efa entero y justo tendrás, para que se prolonguen tus días sobre la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da.
es.B: Debes tener pesas completas y honradas, y medidas completas y honradas, para que vivas mucho tiempo en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da.
es.R: Tus pesas y tus medidas deben ser honradas y del tamaño correcto. Así vivirás mucho tiempo en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da.

fr.L: Tu auras une pierre entière et juste ; tu auras un épha entier et juste, afin que tes jours se prolongent sur la terre que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne.
fr.B: Tu dois avoir des poids exacts et honnêtes, et des mesures exactes et honnêtes, afin de vivre longtemps dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne.
fr.R: Tes poids et tes mesures doivent être honnêtes et de la bonne taille. Alors tu vivras longtemps dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne.

sw.L: Utakuwa na jiwe kamili na la haki; utakuwa na efa kamili na ya haki, ili siku zako ziwe nyingi katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa.
sw.B: Utakuwa na mawe ya kupimia yaliyo kamili na ya haki, na vipimo vilivyo kamili na vya haki, ili uishi siku nyingi katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa.
sw.R: Mawe yako ya kupimia na vipimo vyako lazima viwe vya haki na vya ukubwa unaofaa. Ndipo utaishi muda mrefu katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa.

decisions.choice: full and right: whole and accurate
decisions.reason: "Full" means complete, with nothing taken off. "Right" is the word for righteousness and justice: a weight that is what it claims to be. Honesty in trade is a matter of justice before God (Leviticus 19:35-36; Proverbs 11:1).

decisions.choice: so that your days may be long on the land
decisions.reason: Long life in the land is the promise attached to honoring father and mother (5:16) and to keeping the commandments (4:40; 6:2). Here it is tied to honest weights: daily fairness in trade is part of the life God blesses in the land.

decisions.choice: honest
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "honest" for "right" (m1), the sense this word has with weights and measures. Literal keeps "right".

decisions.choice: live long
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "live long" for "your days may be long".

source.text: כִּ֧י תוֹעֲבַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ כָּל־עֹ֣שֵׂה אֵ֑לֶּה כֹּ֖ל עֹ֥שֵׂה עָֽוֶל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: For [an] abomination of Yahweh your God [is] every [one] doing these, every [one] doing injustice.

en.L: For an abomination to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [is] everyone who does these [things], everyone who does injustice.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God detests anyone who does such things, anyone who acts dishonestly.
en.R: This is because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God hates it when anyone does these things and cheats others.

es.L: Porque abominación [es] para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios todo el que hace estas [cosas], todo el que hace injusticia.
es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios detesta a cualquiera que hace tales cosas, a cualquiera que actúa con deshonestidad.
es.R: Esto es porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios odia que alguien haga estas cosas y engañe a los demás.

fr.L: Car quiconque fait ces [choses], quiconque commet l’injustice, [est] une abomination pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu.
fr.B: Car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu a en horreur quiconque agit ainsi, quiconque se conduit malhonnêtement.
fr.R: En effet, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu déteste qu’on fasse ces choses et qu’on trompe les autres.

sw.L: Kwa maana kila afanyaye mambo haya, kila atendaye udhalimu, [ni] chukizo kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako.
sw.B: Kwa kuwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anamchukia kabisa mtu yeyote afanyaye mambo kama hayo, yeyote atendaye kwa udanganyifu.
sw.R: Hii ni kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anachukia mtu anapofanya mambo haya na kuwadanganya wengine.

decisions.choice: an abomination: what the LORD finds hateful and rejects
decisions.reason: The word is used for what the LORD cannot accept: idolatry (12:31; 13:15), flawed sacrifices (17:1), and here dishonest trade. Proverbs 11:1 and 20:10, 23 say the same of false weights.

decisions.choice: injustice: wrong done to others, here in trade
decisions.reason: The word means unfairness or wrongdoing. The second phrase widens "these things" to every kind of cheating.

decisions.choice: the LORD your God detests / hates it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "an abomination to the LORD" into a verb with the LORD as its subject, and Readable names the injustice as cheating.

source.text: זָכ֕וֹר אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה לְךָ֖ עֲמָלֵ֑ק בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ בְּצֵאתְכֶ֥ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: Remember what did to you Amalek on the way when you came out from Egypt,

en.L: Remember what Amalek did to you on the way when you came out from Egypt,
en.B: Remember what Amalek did to you on your journey out of Egypt,
en.R: Remember what the Amalekites did to you while you were traveling out of Egypt.

es.L: Recuerda lo que te hizo Amalec en el camino, cuando {{plural_you:salieron|salisteis}} de Egipto,
es.B: Recuerda lo que te hizo Amalec durante el viaje, cuando {{plural_you:salían|salíais}} de Egipto,
es.R: Recuerda lo que te hicieron los amalecitas mientras {{plural_you:viajaban|viajabais}} al salir de Egipto.

fr.L: Souviens-toi de ce que t’a fait Amalek en chemin, quand vous êtes sortis d’Égypte,
fr.B: Souviens-toi de ce que t’a fait Amalek pendant votre route au sortir de l’Égypte,
fr.R: Souviens-toi de ce que les Amalécites t’ont fait pendant que vous voyagiez après votre sortie d’Égypte.

sw.L: Kumbuka yale Amaleki aliyokutendea njiani, mlipotoka Misri,
sw.B: Kumbuka yale Amaleki aliyokutendea mlipokuwa safarini kutoka Misri,
sw.R: Kumbuka yale Waamaleki waliyokutendea mlipokuwa mkisafiri kutoka Misri.

decisions.choice: Amalek: the attack at Rephidim
decisions.reason: Amalek was a people of the southern desert, named for a grandson of Esau (Genesis 36:12). They attacked Israel at Rephidim, soon after the crossing of the sea, and the LORD said that he would blot out the memory of Amalek (Exodus 17:8-16). This verse begins the command that closes the chapter.

decisions.choice: remember: a command to keep the event in mind and act on it
decisions.reason: The verb stands in a form that commands. Israel is to remember, and verse 19 says what that memory must lead to.

decisions.choice: the Amalekites
decisions.reason: Readable names the people as "the Amalekites" for "Amalek", the name of their ancestor used for the whole people, and ends the sentence here.

decisions.choice: "te hizo", then "{{plural_you:salieron|salisteis}}"
decisions.reason: Israel is "you" in the singular in the command, but the Hebrew turns to the plural for "when you came out"; the Spanish follows it, with the plural_you span on that verb only.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֨ר קָֽרְךָ֜ בַּדֶּ֗רֶךְ וַיְזַנֵּ֤ב בְּךָ֙ כָּל־הַנֶּחֱשָׁלִ֣ים אַֽחַרֶ֔יךָוְאַתָּ֖ה עָיֵ֣ף וְיָגֵ֑עַ וְלֹ֥א יָרֵ֖א אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: how he met you on the way and attacked in the rear among you all the stragglers behind you, and you [were] faint and weary, and not he feared God.

en.L: how he met you on the way and attacked your rear, all the stragglers behind you, when you were faint and weary; and he did not fear God.
en.B: how they met you on the road when you were tired and worn out and struck at your rear, cutting down all who were lagging behind. They had no fear of God.
en.R: They came out against you on the road. You were tired and worn out. They attacked from behind and killed the people who could not keep up. They did not respect God at all.

es.L: cómo te salió al encuentro en el camino y atacó tu retaguardia, a todos los rezagados detrás de ti, cuando tú estabas cansado y agotado; y no temió a Dios.
es.B: cómo te salieron al paso en el camino cuando estabas cansado y agotado, y atacaron tu retaguardia, abatiendo a todos los que se quedaban atrás. No tenían ningún temor de Dios.
es.R: Salieron contra ti en el camino. Tú estabas cansado y agotado. Atacaron por detrás y mataron a los que no podían seguir el paso. No tenían ningún respeto por Dios.

fr.L: comment il t’a rencontré en chemin et a frappé ton arrière-garde, tous les traînards derrière toi, quand tu étais las et épuisé ; et il n’a pas craint Dieu.
fr.B: comment ils t’ont surpris sur la route, alors que tu étais fatigué et épuisé, et ont attaqué tes arrières, abattant tous ceux qui traînaient derrière. Ils n’avaient aucune crainte de Dieu.
fr.R: Ils sont sortis contre toi sur la route. Tu étais fatigué et épuisé. Ils ont attaqué par-derrière et ont tué les gens qui n’arrivaient pas à suivre. Ils n’avaient aucun respect pour Dieu.

sw.L: jinsi alivyokukuta njiani na kuwapiga walio nyuma yako, wote waliokuwa wakijikokota nyuma yako, ulipokuwa umezimia na kuchoka; wala hakumcha Mungu.
sw.B: jinsi walivyokukuta njiani ulipokuwa umechoka na kulegea, wakashambulia upande wako wa nyuma, wakawaua wote waliokuwa wakichelewa nyuma. Hawakuwa na hofu ya Mungu.
sw.R: Walikujia njiani. Ulikuwa umechoka sana. Walishambulia kutoka nyuma na kuwaua watu walioshindwa kwenda pamoja na wengine. Hawakumheshimu Mungu hata kidogo.

decisions.choice: attacked in the rear: struck at the tail of the column
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for "tail". Amalek fell on the back of the marching people, where the weak, the old and the tired were.

decisions.choice: he did not fear God: Amalek did not fear God
decisions.reason: The subject is Amalek, as in the rest of the verse. Attacking the helpless showed that Amalek had no fear of God, who protects the weak. The words could also be read of Israel in its weariness, but the sentence speaks of what Amalek did.

decisions.choice: faint and weary: worn out by the journey
decisions.reason: The two words say the same thing twice, for emphasis. Exodus 17:1-7 tells how the people had just suffered thirst on the way.

decisions.choice: they / them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "they" for the people of Amalek, where the Hebrew uses "he" for the people under its ancestor's name, as verse 17.

decisions.choice: killed the people who could not keep up
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the attack on the stragglers did.

source.text: וְהָיָ֡ה בְּהָנִ֣יחַ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֣יךָ׀לְ֠ךָ מִכָּל־אֹ֨יְבֶ֜יךָ מִסָּבִ֗יב בָּאָ֨רֶץ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְהוָֽה־אֱ֠לֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵ֨ן לְךָ֤ נַחֲלָה֙ לְרִשְׁתָּ֔הּ תִּמְחֶה֙ אֶת־זֵ֣כֶר עֲמָלֵ֔ק מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם לֹ֖א תִּשְׁכָּֽח׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, when gives rest Yahweh your God to you from all your enemies round about in the land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you [as an] inheritance to possess it, you will wipe out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens; not you will forget.

en.L: And it shall be, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you rest from all your enemies all around, in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you [as] an inheritance to take possession of it, you shall wipe out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens. You shall not forget.
en.B: So when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you rest from all the enemies around you in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you to possess as an inheritance, you must wipe out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens. Do not forget.
en.R: So when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God gives you peace from all your enemies around you in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you to be your own, you must wipe out every trace of Amalek from the earth. Do not forget!

es.L: Y será, cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te haya dado descanso de todos tus enemigos alrededor, en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da [como] herencia para tomar posesión de ella, que borrarás la memoria de Amalec de debajo de los cielos. No lo olvidarás.
es.B: Así que, cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te haya dado descanso de todos los enemigos que te rodean en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da en herencia para que la poseas, deberás borrar la memoria de Amalec de debajo del cielo. No lo olvides.
es.R: Así que, cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te dé paz frente a todos los enemigos que te rodean en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da para que sea tuya, tienes que borrar todo rastro de Amalec de la tierra. ¡No lo olvides!

fr.L: Et il arrivera, quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’aura donné du repos face à tous tes ennemis d’alentour, dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne [en] héritage pour en prendre possession, que tu effaceras le souvenir d’Amalek de dessous les cieux. Tu n’oublieras pas.
fr.B: Ainsi, quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’aura donné du repos face à tous les ennemis qui t’entourent, dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne en héritage pour que tu en prennes possession, tu effaceras le souvenir d’Amalek de dessous les cieux. N’oublie pas.
fr.R: Alors, quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’aura donné la paix face à tous tes ennemis autour de toi, dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne pour qu’il soit à toi, tu devras effacer toute trace d’Amalek de la terre. N’oublie pas !

sw.L: Na itakuwa, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakapokuwa amekupa pumziko kutoka kwa adui zako wote wanaokuzunguka, katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa [iwe] urithi ili uimiliki, utaifuta kumbukumbu ya Amaleki chini ya mbingu. Usisahau.
sw.B: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakapokuwa amekupa pumziko kutoka kwa adui wote wanaokuzunguka katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa uimiliki kuwa urithi, utaifuta kumbukumbu ya Amaleki chini ya mbingu. Usisahau.
sw.R: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakapokupa amani mbele ya adui zako wote wanaokuzunguka katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa iwe yako, lazima ufute kila alama ya Amaleki duniani. Usisahau!

decisions.choice: rest: an end to war, secure life in the land
decisions.reason: "Rest" is safety from enemies after the land is settled (12:10; Joshua 21:44; 2 Samuel 7:1). The command against Amalek is for that time, not for the march into the land.

decisions.choice: wipe out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens: destroy Amalek so that it is no more
decisions.reason: "From under the heavens" means from anywhere on earth. The words echo the LORD's own oath in Exodus 17:14. 1 Samuel 15:2-3 tells how Saul was later sent to carry out this command, and Esther 3:1 names Haman as a descendant of Agag, Amalek's king, still an enemy of Israel.

decisions.choice: do not forget: the memory itself is a duty
decisions.reason: The command both begins and ends with memory (verse 17). Israel is to hold in mind what was done to the weak on the way out of Egypt. The judgment on Amalek is God's sentence on a people who preyed on the helpless and did not fear him (verse 18).

decisions.choice: peace / every trace
decisions.reason: Readable says "peace" for "rest" from enemies (m1) and "every trace of Amalek" for "the memory of Amalek", and "from the earth" for "from under the heavens" (m2).
